boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten purchase-free places where Elizabethtown College students can talk, study, play games, exercise, or unwind together.

cards.title: Bring Lunch to the Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: A student-only room in Baugher Student Center 246
cards.notes: Pack lunch, claim a table with another commuter, and use the refrigerator or microwave instead of buying food on campus.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-only meetup room equipped for bring-your-own meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College identifies the Commuter Lounge as a place for commuters to study, relax, and socialize and says it includes a refrigerator, microwave, and Keurig for their use.
cards.access_notes: Located in Baugher Student Center room 246; access requires an Elizabethtown College ID and is limited to commuter students.

cards.title: Reset Together at The Well
cards.subtitle: A quiet space on the Bowers Center’s second floor
cards.notes: Meet a friend upstairs for a quiet reset between classes; keep the conversation low so the room remains restorative.
cards.short_summary: A campus wellness space suited to a calm, no-spend pause.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists The Well among places where commuters can spend time and states that it has a quiet space on the Bowers Center’s second floor.
cards.access_notes: For Elizabethtown College students; enter through the Bowers Center and follow current building-access rules.

cards.title: Start a Ping-Pong Match in The Bird Cage
cards.subtitle: Games and lounge seating inside Baugher Student Center
cards.notes: Bring a classmate for pool or ping-pong, or settle near the television for an easy indoor hang between commitments.
cards.short_summary: A common room where conversation and table games share the space.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College describes The Bird Cage as a common room for relaxing and studying, equipped with pool and ping-pong tables and a large television.
cards.access_notes: Inside Baugher Student Center and intended for the campus community; observe current building-access requirements.

cards.title: Share a Study Table at High Library
cards.subtitle: The library’s conversation-friendly first floor
cards.notes: Gather on the first floor for collaborative research or parallel work, saving quieter library areas for silent study.
cards.short_summary: A library floor where students can research and work without strict silence.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says High Library’s first floor is not a quiet space and provides students with room to research and get work done.
cards.access_notes: Campus buildings are not generally open to the public; this hang is for students and other authorized library users.

cards.title: Walk Laps in the Field House
cards.subtitle: Indoor track time with equipment checkout nearby
cards.notes: Invite a friend for conversational laps on the indoor track, or borrow available sports equipment for a casual session.
cards.short_summary: An indoor movement break that needs neither admission nor purchased gear.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists the Bowers Center Field House as a place where commuters can exercise and says it has an indoor track and sports equipment available for checkout.
cards.access_notes: For eligible Elizabethtown College users; building entry and equipment checkout may require a College ID.

cards.title: Toss a Frisbee on Brinser Field
cards.subtitle: Open grass beside Wolf Field and Brossman Commons
cards.notes: Bring a Frisbee or simply spread out on the grass with friends; yield whenever the field is reserved for organized use.
cards.short_summary: A central lawn for an informal game or relaxed group meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College describes Brinser Field as a large, centrally located grassy field suitable for multiple outdoor activities.
cards.access_notes: The College says outdoor campus spaces are open to the public unless access is restricted; scheduled field use takes priority.

cards.title: Claim a Picnic Table on Academic Quad
cards.subtitle: Central campus lawn beside Brossman Commons
cards.notes: Meet at the picnic tables or Adirondack chairs for conversation, card games, or outdoor studying in fair weather.
cards.short_summary: A central green with ready-made seating for an outdoor group break.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies Academic Quad as a large central grassy area with picnic tables near Thompson Gymnasium and Adirondack chairs near Esbenshade Hall.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space is normally open to students and the public, subject to temporary College restrictions or scheduled events.

cards.title: Set Up a Group Session in The Learning Zone
cards.subtitle: Dedicated study space on Brossman Commons’ second floor
cards.notes: Bring one shared task and work through it together; choose another location if your discussion would disrupt nearby study.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated indoor study area for classmates working side by side.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College lists The Learning Zone among places commuters can study, relax, or socialize and locates its dedicated study space on Brossman Commons’ second floor.
cards.access_notes: For Elizabethtown College students and authorized guests; follow current Brossman Commons access rules.

cards.title: Study Beside the Mineral Gallery
cards.subtitle: Atrium seating inside the Masters Center entrance
cards.notes: Choose a table or lounge chair near the gallery, compare notes with a classmate, and leave exhibition objects untouched.
cards.short_summary: A science-building atrium combining seating with a visible mineral display.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says the atrium between Musser Hall and the Masters Center Mineral Gallery has tables, chairs, and lounge seating used by students of all majors.
cards.access_notes: Located just inside the Masters Center main entrance; academic buildings are limited to students, employees, and invited guests.

cards.title: Co-Work Quietly in Nicarry Hall
cards.subtitle: An all-student lounge on Nicarry’s second floor
cards.notes: Meet for silent co-working, agree on a check-in time, and move conversation elsewhere to preserve the lounge’s quiet use.
cards.short_summary: A quiet second-floor lounge open to students from every major.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College states that all students can use the quiet study lounge on the second floor of Nicarry Hall.
cards.access_notes: Available to Elizabethtown College students; Nicarry Hall is not a public-access building.
